issues.title: What's new in RubyGems and Bundler 4.1
issues.html:
#​826 — November 12, 2026


Read on the Web



Ruby Weekly





Metaprogramming on a Budget — A "peek behind the curtain of Rails' metaprogramming magic!" Active Record generates 21 methods for every column, which could eat a lot of memory, but a little define_method trick allows methods to share compiled instruction sequences…

Hartley McGuire (Rails at Scale)



💡 The follow-up Hartley mentions at the end has just been merged: Aaron Patterson's PR stores Active Record attributes in an array so reader methods can be shared by column position, with the reading of attributes getting up to 1.3x faster.



Leaving New Relic? No NRQL, No Regex, No API Calls Required — AppSignal skips the query language: tags filter in the UI, deploy markers work out of the box, and sensitive data is scrubbed with a simple denylist. Errors, N+1s, Sidekiq and logs in one Ruby gem. Unlimited users, 30-day trial.

AppSignal sponsor



What's New in RubyGems and Bundler 4.1 — RubyGems' maintainer wraps up a three-part tour of version 4.1, currently in beta. In this final part, Hiroshi focuses on gem install's improved efficiency, but if you want to go back, part 1 covers override (to rewrite version constraints) and prune (for cleaning up after installs), and part 2 focuses on supply chain defenses like cooldown.

Hiroshi Shibata



⚡️ IN BRIEF:

  • 🇺🇸 Those earlybird tickets for RubyConf 2027 (in Portland next May) we mentioned last week are now on sale! Also, Blue Ridge Ruby is returning to Asheville on April 29-30 and the CFP is open until January 29.

  • 🔒 Rails 8.0 left security support on November 7, making last week's 8.0.5.2 its final fix. Rails 8.1 is covered until October 2027. I hope 8.2 is out by then…! 😅

  • 🔒 Earlier this month, a malicious gem called strutil-core ran a credential-stealing worm at gem install time via its extconf.rb. RubyGems pulled it within hours and Socket knows of no victims.

  • 📘 Eustáquio Rangel has been updating Brazil's first Ruby book for over 20 years. It's now in English as Meet Ruby, a "live book" that keeps evolving with the language, and covers fundamentals through to Ractors and RubyLLM.

  • The Bridgetown Ruby site generator is looking for sponsors to help keep development going.



Releasing Gems with OIDC and GitHub Actions — Releasing a gem has always involved numerous steps and modern security concerns have added a few more… but automation can help. ruby-gem-release does it all from a GitHub Actions workflow, using Trusted Publishing so no RubyGems API key is needed.

Daniel Doubrovkine



Hand-Coding a Feature in a Ruby Gem — After a year off from technical blogging, Felipe comes back with a tale of adding a feature to his personal reading log gem and the benefits he got from not using AI.

Felipe Vogel



A Closer Look at the Critical Active Storage ImageMagick Issue — Greg reproduces the 9.8-rated bug fixed in last week's Rails releases by showing how crafted uploads can expose files like master.key in a vulnerable app using MiniMagick and local disk storage.

Greg Molnar



🚨 Rails 8.0 Support Has Ended. Get Your Upgrade on Autopilot — Join the beta to get access to our AI agent + a free 8.1 readiness check; get small green PRs you can review and merge.

FastRuby.io® | AI-native Rails Maintenance sponsor



📄 Drawing an SVG Sky Map with Ruby and Astronoby – Plot the sky for any date and place with a star catalogue and a little trigonometry. Rémy Hannequin

📄 Going All-In on Sorbet: Typing an Entire Rails App in Four Days Nathan Broadbent (DocSpring)

🤖 How Can You Be Responsible for Code You Don't Understand? David Bryant Copeland

📄 Writing Ruby Extensions in Odin Michael Kohl



🛠 Code & Tools



🤖 RubyLLM 2.2: Sandboxed Code Execution, Skills, and More — The AI framework now lets models run code they write in a sandbox (using Bubblewrap on Linux or macOS's native sandbox). Also new are skills, tools that can pause to ask questions, and four more providers. What's New in 2.2 has the full laundry list!

Carmine Paolino



Deleting Old Rows Shouldn’t Be Your Slowest Rake Task — TimescaleDB drops old data by the chunk, no bloat. Same Postgres, same ActiveRecord. $1000 credit on Tiger Cloud.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



Panko 1.0: The Fast JSON Serializer Drops Its C Extension — Panko made its name as a fast JSON serializer that shipped a C extension, but v1.0 goes for a pure Ruby engine that compiles each serializer into code YJIT can optimize (and it's now faster in most cases too). More on its design here.

Yosi Attias



protostar: Protocol Buffers in Pure Ruby — A "slightly unhinged" take on protobufs that compiles .proto files without protoc. It's slower than native and experimental, but passes protobuf's conformance suite.

Julik Tarkhanov



  • Minitest 6.1 – Adds abstract_test_case! for base test classes and supports Prism 2.0. There's also now an official AI policy which is… "just NO".

  • rspec-rails 8.1 – Now officially supports Rails 8.1. The dev branch already supports Rails 8.2, too, if you need that.

  • Facets 4.1 – The veteran core extensions library now aligns several overlapping methods with Active Support 8.1.

  • Stripe Ruby 21.0 – API keys are no longer kept in Marshal or YAML dumps of Stripe objects.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem





  • A few months ago we linked to Rémi Mercier's project to create a Ruby-themed stained glass panel and it's now almost ready for sale. Along the way, he's been blogging about how it's coming together, including the design of its lighting stand.

  • 🎥 Paul Irish's chrome-capture records Chrome tabs directly to MP4 at 60+ FPS, including audio. Could be handy for recording app demos or reproducing bugs, and no ffmpeg is required.

  • 🤖 Chrome's Modern Web Guidance has reached 1.0, giving coding agents access to browser compatibility data, HTML, CSS and accessibility advice, and frontend best practices.

  • 🔎 Betterleaks, started by Gitleaks' original creator, is a Go-powered tool to scan Git repos for leaked secrets.

issues.title: Patch Rails now: 21 security fixes in one release
issues.html:
#​825 — November 5, 2026


Read on the Web



Ruby Weekly





🔒 Rails 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 Released to Fix 21 Security Issues — A rare 21-advisory release, led by a critical Active Storage bug (when using ImageMagick/mini_magick) where attaching a specially crafted image can let an uploader write (and sometimes read) arbitrary files. A Strong Parameters bypass, remote_ip spoofing in 8.1, and more make this a key update.

Mike Dalessio (Rails Core)



💡 Christine Seeman's walkthrough covers the advisories you may want to give a closer look, what can break on upgrade, and workarounds if you can't upgrade.



🚨 Rails 8.0 Security Support Ends Nov 7. Upgrade with AI — Our AI agent works on your own CI and opens small PRs only when your suite is green. It dual-boots with `next_rails`. Nothing merges without your review. Join the beta waitlist and get a free Rails 8.1 readiness check.

FastRuby.io® | AI-native Rails Maintenance sponsor



Moment of Ruby: An Argument for Nothing — How can you tell "no argument was supplied" from an explicit nil or false without a sentinel constant? Here's a cute, small Ruby idiom to do it.

Chris Zempel (Aha!)



⚡️ IN BRIEF:

  • 📘 Programming Ruby 4, the sixth edition of the Pickaxe, is now in print!

  • 🇺🇸 RubyConf 2027 is heading to Portland, Oregon on May 24-26, with early-bird tickets going on sale November 11.

  • On Ruby 4.0, defining a method in a module costs more for each class that includes it, up to 4x slower than 3.4. Rails route helpers, in particular, run into this, and a backport to 4.0 has been requested.

  • 🇧🇪 Ruby is returning to FOSDEM with a 'Ruby Beyond Rails'-themed devroom on January 30 in Brussels. The CFP closes December 1.

  • RubyMine 2026.3, JetBrains' popular commercial Ruby IDE, has been released.



⚠️ Trilogy Fixes an SQL Injection in Rails' Favored MySQL Client — Trilogy, the MySQL client GitHub built and Rails recommends, had a 9.3-rated SQL injection vulnerability which has been fixed and requires an upgrade to v2.13.2+, if you're using it. Greg Molnar built a vulnerable app to see how bad the vulnerability is and found it's worse than he first thought.

Trilogy maintainers



🔒 It's a busy time for security releases, so I've included a section at the end of the issue rounding up some releases that have landed to fix numerous vulnerabilities.



A Look at Lemans, the Harness Behind the Agents on Rails Benchmark — A tour of the Ruby harness Evil Martians built for the Rails Foundation's coding agent benchmark, plus some fun in how agents have tried to cheat at it…

Dementyev and Petrov (Evil Martians)



Don't Make a Human Do What AI Is Amazing At — John shares Nunebot, the markdown prompt he uses to sweep his apps and gems, pick one fix per repo, prove the fix with a failing-then-passing test, and open a PR.

John Nunemaker



💡 Along similar lines, David Bryant Copeland asks why review AI-generated code at all, arguing the effort is better spent on tooling that catches problems mechanically.



Painless Web Scraping With The New SerpApi's Extract API — Scrape any public webpage or add search to your Ruby application with one developer-friendly API built by Ruby engineers.

SerpApi sponsor



📄 Modernizing a Rails App from 2018 – How an ancient Rails 5 app was ported by moving it into a fresh app rather than upgrading in place. I did an upgrade the hard way recently, and I don't blame them! Kevin Campusano

📺 When Rails Met Fibers: Migrating Sidekick from Puma to Falcon – A 42-minute keynote on moving Shopify's AI assistant onto Falcon. Williams, Lawhorn and Barnes

📄 When Two Background Jobs Target the Same Record – A lost-update reproduction under Solid Queue, and a look at where to fix it. Syed Aslam

📄 IP-Based Route Restrictions on Heroku with Rails Daniela Baron

📺 DHH's Kaigi on Rails 2026 Keynote: Where the Tracks Go Next



🛠 Code & Tools





Spinel 2026.10.25: Matz's Ruby Compiler Continues to Advance — The second dated release of Matz's ahead-of-time Ruby-to-native compiler brings in a ton of stuff since I reviewed it six months ago! It's faster, offers a new WASM target, supports more of the standard library, and strings now behave as single shared objects like in CRuby. It's a great time to play with it!

Yukihiro Matsumoto



💡 Stan Lo's new, one-page Spinel intro rounds the project up generally, and explains how it differs to CRuby, what it can't compile, and its ruby-bench results.



group_by_day Shouldn't Time Out on Your Biggest Table — TimescaleDB extends Postgres so daily counts stay fast on huge tables. Same ActiveRecord. Get $1000 credit.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



JRuby 10.1.3.0 Released with Many Fixes and Improvements — A big release for JRuby's Ruby 4.0-compatible line. Mutex, Queue and sockets now go through the Fiber scheduler, method and branch coverage are implemented (so SimpleCov's branch mode can work), and Prism is now merged into JRuby itself.

JRuby Team



💡 JRuby 10.0.8.0 also landed for those on the Ruby 3.4-compatible line.



Duel: Fail CI When Your Code Gets Slower — Runs your benchmarks on two versions of your code side by side and fails if the new code is slower.

Erik Berlin



QueryStash: Cache Hot, Slow-Changing Queries Below Active Record — Caches lookups of your choosing across requests at the adapter level (so your calls don't need to change) with TTLs calculated from each result.

Persona



rails-query-command: Use Rails 8.2's bin/rails query on 7.2 to 8.1 — A backport of Rails 8.2's forthcoming bin/rails query command that runs on older Rails versions. It runs Active Record expressions or SQL with database-write protection and returns paginated JSON, which is ideal for agents and scripts.

Lázaro Nixon



TaskProgress: Progress Bars for Task Trees, from Terminal to Browser — Track nested task trees spread across threads, Fibers, subprocesses and Ractors (on Ruby 4) and render them to a terminal/log/browser with SSE/Turbo.

Julik Tarkhanov



  • RubyGems and Bundler 4.0.24 – Bundler can now read the Ruby version from mise.toml's inline table form and reports which locked gems can't be materialized on your platform.

  • Ferrum 0.20 and Cuprite 0.20 – The Chrome/CDP driver and its Capybara adapter add page.console message collection and real Logger support.

  • Grover 2.0 – Security release for the library that transforms HTML into PDFs, PNGs or JPEGs using Puppeteer and Chromium.

  • Net::SSH 8.1 – Three breaking changes, including no interactive prompts when stdin isn't a TTY.



📰 Classifieds



More AI commits and more test runs mean more waiting. WarpBuild runs your Ruby CI 2x faster at half the cost. Get $50 in free credits with START50.

🔺 Made a library? Written a blog post? Found a useful tutorial? Share it with the Ruby community on RubyFlow, the Ruby and Rails community linklog.



⚠️ A recent wave of Ruby security news



  • Following the regexp fixes we covered in our emergency issue, k0kubun has asked Ruby core to decide whether compiling untrusted strings into a Regexp should be supported at all, and if so, to request CVEs for them. It goes to the November 12 dev meeting. Meanwhile, Infield shows how to probe an end-of-life Ruby for the bugs.

  • A dozen advisories have hit Ruby's HTML sanitizing stack: Loofah 2.25.3, Nokogiri 1.19.5+, rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.2 and Sanitize 7.0.2. The big one is a mutation XSS in Loofah's HTML5 scrubbers that affects the default allowlist.

  • Rack 3.2.8, 3.1.23 and 2.2.25 fix four issues, the biggest being a multipart parser that retained parsed data in its scan buffer, so a malicious upload could exhaust memory.

  • Addressable 2.9.1 ships fixes for seven advisories, two of them reported by Ruby Central's new gem security effort.

  • v0.9.2 of the brotli gem bundles the patched Brotli 1.2.1, closing an actively exploited decoder RCE that's recently hit Node and browsers.

  • Ransack 6.0.1 (plus 5.0.3 and 4.4.4) stops sort_link passing URL options like script_name through from params, an open redirect and XSS.

issues.title: How fast can you actually patch Ruby?
issues.html:
#​824 — October 29, 2026


Read on the Web



🔒 Last Friday we sent out a special issue about some CRuby security releases which fixed a few nasty regexp bugs. If you haven't updated yet, it's worth a read to see if you're affected and what to check!
__
Your editor, Peter Cooper



Ruby Weekly





How Fast Can You Actually Patch Ruby? — When the Ruby security fixes shipped last week, Dennis timed how long they took to reach version managers, Docker images, CI services and hosts. The core team's image took eight minutes, while Docker's official image (Rails and Kamal's default) took ~16 hours.

Dennis Paagman



💡 Things are improving, though, as Ruby core team members now have commit access to Docker's Ruby image repo and are looking into automating updates. Meanwhile, Greg Molnar shows how to build your own image locally and deploy it with Kamal.



Your Dashboard Shouldn’t Wait for a Cron Job — The nightly job rolls up yesterday’s rows so the dashboard loads. Numbers lag a day and the job keeps growing. TimescaleDB continuous aggregates refresh rollups inside Postgres, so ActiveRecord reads fresh totals. Get $1000 credit to start.

Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor



Bad Requests and the Dream of a Quiet Rails App — Requests for /.env and /wp-admin, binary bytes in User-Agent headers, made-up MIME types… Ben walks through the Rails middleware stack to show why some junk requests become 500s, and why even 'handled' ones can still set off your error monitor.

Ben Sheldon



What's New at RubyGems.org: Ruby Central's Changelog Returns — Ruby Central catches us up on RubyGems.org and Bundler 4.1 work. Its AI scans of popular gems are a highlight: reviewers rejected 90% of the findings they looked into, though one was a critical auth bypass in rubyntlm.

Kirk Haines (Ruby Central)



Thank You, But I Prefer It My Way — If an LLM can just rewrite a library, is it worth persuading a maintainer about your PR or do you just route around it? Julik ponders the complexities and offers some practical ways forward.

Julik Tarkhanov



I Get 215 GitHub Notifications a Day, So I Built a Bot to Triage Them — A look at how the creator of RubyLLM built a RubyLLM-powered agent to label issues and PRs, reply only when useful, and sort the rest onto a board.

Carmine Paolino



📄 Parsing JSON-Structured Docker Logs with the OpenTelemetry Collector – How 37signals unwraps the JSON-in-JSON logs from its Kamal-deployed Rails apps. Lewis Buckley (37signals)

📄 Benchmarking Campfire with Many Users – Sam load-tests Campfire with up to 3,000 users, opens three PRs, and compares Rails with his Roundhouse-transpiled build on Falcon. Sam Ruby

📄 React Server Components on a Gumroad Fork: From 53 to 86 on Mobile PageSpeed – Compares live RSC and Inertia versions of a product page, using the commercial React on Rails Pro. Justin Gordon (ShakaCode)

📄 Making AI Agents Safe to Retry – Moving an LLM agent into a Sidekiq job without retries repeating its actions. Mateus Pereira (FastRuby.io)



🛠 Code & Tools





Carton: Real Boundaries for Ruby — Built on Ruby 4's experimental Ruby::Box, Carton enforces module boundaries at runtime where only what a 'carton' exports is visible outside it, monkey patches to core classes stay contained, and each carton can bring its own gem versions.

David Cristofaro



🚨 Rails 8.0 Support Ends Nov 7 | Get AI Upgrades on Autopilot — Our AI agent ships small upgrade PRs that pass your tests; nothing merges without you. Join the beta waitlist.

FastRuby.io® | AI-Native Rails Maintenance sponsor



Spree 6.0: A Rewrite of the Rails E-Commerce Platform — Marketplace, B2B, tax and inventory features are now in the open source core, carts and orders are separate models, and the checkout state machines are gone. Note that Rails now powers only the backend, with a React admin and Next.js storefront.

Spree Commerce



GenevaDrive: Durable, Step-Based Workflows for Rails — Define multi-step workflows tied to a record, with waits, resumable steps over large collections, and signals from webhooks. State lives in your database, with steps surviving restarts and duplicate job runs being skipped.

Julik Tarkhanov



⏱️ Horologium: Scientific Time Library for Ruby — A new gem, extracted from Astronoby, that handles eight time scales including TAI, TT, TDB, UTC and UT1, plus leap seconds (which Time can't represent) and precise Julian dates.

Rémy Hannequin



  • ⭐ RubyGems and Bundler 4.1.0.beta3 renames Bundler's new override keys to in: and with:, and records overrides in a new OVERRIDES section of Gemfile.lock.

  • Prosopite 2.5 – N+1 query detector. Now suggests fixes, adds RSpec and Minitest assertions, and can ignore known N+1s while you adopt it gradually.

  • OmniAuth 2.2 / 2.3 – Multi-provider auth. The first new minor versions since 2022 add allowed_hosts and support for concurrent sign-ins.

  • The Git Gem 6.0 – Ruby interface to the git command line. A big breaking release that removes the old object model and requires Git 2.43+.

  • ruby-duckdb 2.0 – Ruby client for the DuckDB analytical database, now tracking DuckDB 2.0 and dropping several deprecated APIs.

  • Rage 1.29 – Fiber-based, Rails-compatible API framework, now ready for Ruby 4.1's fiber scheduler changes.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • Sean Goedecke argues that software is slow because of bad design, not slow languages, drawing on his experience of staring at Ruby flamegraphs and profiling Rails endpoints.

  • Nate Berkopec ported Ruby 4.0.9 to Fil-C, a memory-safe C toolchain. It ran real programs like Puma, but was ~5x slower and used far more memory, so Nate has 𝕏 declared the experiment over.

  • Python's experimental JIT is likely to be removed. Ruby came up a lot in the related Hacker News thread, where Jean Boussier credited Matz for supporting work on Ruby's JITs.

  • Sentry has given $1m to open source maintainers this year, up from $750k, with $40,000 going to Ruby Central.
